newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling rates stuck in matching market.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling rates stuck in matching market.

text.p: NAIROBI, JAN 15 (REUTER) - Kenya's shilling rates held within a narrow band of 54.60/70 as demand matched supply, commercial bank dealers said.
They said the market was near steady, with very little interest from either side.
"This is January. Most Kenyans are still setting their goals for the year," one dealer said. "Business should pick up from the second month," he added.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 54.66 from 54.67 against the dollar. Against the pound, it was unchanged at a mean of 91.48.
Another dealer said some inflows from the agricultural sector hardly affected the market.
The money market was liquid. Most banks appeared to have an excess, as a result of amounts brought forward from last year when most banks built up their reserves before the new year.

Overnight rates were quoted between 7 and 10 percent from Tuesday's 10-percent levels. Commercial bank dealers said they expected rates to move up within the next two weeks because many banks were expected to borrow to build up cash-ratio deposits.
